On the full set, EM is diluted by trivial agreement: instances where all $N$ samples produce identical (possibly incorrect) outputs receive EM${=}1$ regardless of quality, compressing the signal's dynamic range.
On the conditional set---where the model demonstrably produces varied outputs---exact agreement becomes the strongest quality signal.
The margin over SJ is largest on RE ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.171$), where compound extraction decisions amplify output variability, and smallest on CoNLL LLaMA ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.002$), where all signals converge near $\rho{\approx}0.46$.

Table~\ref{tab:wnut} reports all five signals on WNUT-17.
VC achieves $\rho{=}0.724$ (AUROC${=}0.913$) on the full set, but conditional analysis (non-zero F1 instances) reveals this is entirely driven by the zero/non-zero boundary: conditional $\rho{=}0.038$ ($p{=}0.49$).
LP shows the reverse pattern: full-set $\rho{=}{-}0.410$ but conditional $\rho{=}0.350$, the highest among all signals on the conditional set.
This inversion confirms that full-set correlations on high-failure-rate datasets conflate binary success prediction with quality gradation.

1	\section{Experiments}
2	\label{sec:experiments}
3	
4	\subsection{Experimental Setup}
5	\label{sec:setup}
6	
7	\paragraph{Datasets.}
8	We evaluate on three English IE benchmarks spanning a difficulty gradient.
9	\textbf{SciERC} \cite{luan2018scierc} contains 551 test instances annotated for joint NER (6 types) and RE (7 types).
10	\textbf{CoNLL-2003} \cite{tjongkimsang2003conll} provides 3{,}453 test sentences with 4 entity types, where models achieve ${\approx}$91\% micro F1.
11	\textbf{WNUT-17} \cite{derczynski2017wnut} consists of 1{,}287 social media instances with emerging entities, used to probe method boundaries (52\% zero F1).
12	
13	\paragraph{Models and sampling.}
14	Both \textbf{Qwen3-8B} and \textbf{LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct} are fine-tuned with LoRA (rank$=$32, $\alpha{=}64$) for 5 epochs using LLaMA Factory \cite{zheng2024llamafactory} under identical training procedures.
15	Qwen3-8B's SciERC checkpoint has a minor train--test mismatch (empty thinking tokens); a quantitative analysis rules out this confound (Appendix~\ref{app:thinking_token}).
16	We draw $N{=}8$ samples at $T{=}1.0$ (primary), with $N{=}16$ for scaling experiments.\footnote{$N{=}16$ with 3 seeds verifies scaling and ranking stability ($\sigma{\leq}0.026$; Table~\ref{tab:multiseed}); gains beyond $N{=}8$ are sublinear (Appendix~\ref{app:n_scaling}).}
17	Inference uses vLLM with constrained decoding \cite{willard2023guided}.
18	
19	%% ============================================================
20	\subsection{Quality Estimation Results}
21	\label{sec:qe_results}
22	
23	\begin{table*}[t]
24	\centering
25	\small
26	\caption{Quality estimation ($\rho$ and AUROC; $N{=}8$, seed${=}42$, single-seed; 3-seed stability in Table~\ref{tab:multiseed}). Best in \textbf{bold}. $^\dagger$RE results rest on a single benchmark (SciERC, 40\% zero-F1 rate). $N{=}16$ in Table~\ref{tab:robustness}.}
27	\label{tab:quality_estimation}
28	\begin{tabular}{ll cc cc cc cc}
29	\toprule
30	& & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{SciERC NER}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{SciERC RE}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CoNLL (Qwen)}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{\textbf{CoNLL (LLaMA)}} \\
31	\cmidrule(lr){3-4} \cmidrule(lr){5-6} \cmidrule(lr){7-8} \cmidrule(lr){9-10}
32	Signal & Family & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC & $\rho$ & AUC \\

44	Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation} presents $\rho$ and AUROC for five signals across tasks and models.\footnote{$\varepsilon{=}0.05$ applies only to selection (\S\ref{sec:selection_gap}); quality estimation is $\varepsilon$-free. Selection F1 is stable across $\varepsilon \in [0, 0.2]$ (Appendix~\ref{app:epsilon_robustness}).}
45	
46	\paragraph{Signal rankings are difficulty-dependent.}
47	On SciERC NER, structural signals lead (VC $\rho{=}0.379$, SJ $0.360$) over surface ($\rho{\leq}0.295$) and LP ($0.205$); bootstrap CIs confirm the SJ--LP gap ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.155$; Appendix~\ref{app:bootstrap_signal}).
48	On CoNLL (single-sample F1${\approx}$0.91), EM leads both $\rho$ and AUROC ($0.816$); the $\rho$--AUROC dissociation across datasets reflects use-case alignment.
49	On $^\dagger$RE, LP rises above SJ and FK at $N{=}16$ (Table~\ref{tab:multiseed}).
50	At the capability boundary---WNUT-17 (52\% zero F1)---all conditional signals collapse (Table~\ref{tab:wnut}); restricting to non-zero instances reshuffles rankings, with EM strongest on NER ($\rho{=}0.360$) and $^\dagger$RE ($\rho{=}0.417$) while LP $^\dagger$RE collapses to $\rho{=}0.011$ (Figure~\ref{fig:signal_heatmap}, Appendix~\ref{app:additional}).

52	%% ============================================================
53	\subsection{The Correlation-Selection Gap}
54	\label{sec:selection_gap}
55	
56	We define the correlation-selection gap as the disparity between a signal's instance-level rank correlation with F1 and its ability to select the best output from $N$ candidates.
57	
58	\begin{table}[t]
59	\centering
60	\small
61	\caption{Best-of-$N$ selection F1 on SciERC ($N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$). LP is per-sample; others are instance-level. NER: 2-seed mean${\pm}\sigma$, Fisher $p$ vs.\ single-sample; $^\dagger$RE: single seed. Best non-oracle in \textbf{bold}. $^\ddagger$Single: one $T{=}1.0$ draw.}
62	\label{tab:selection}
63	\begin{tabular}{lccc}
64	\toprule
65	Method & NER F1 & $p$ & RE F1 \\
66	\midrule
67	Oracle & $0.778 \pm 0.003$ & --- & 0.585 \\
68	\midrule
69	\multicolumn{4}{l}{\textit{Per-sample signal}} \\
70	LP           & $\mathbf{0.647} \pm 0.005$ & .29 & 0.395 \\
71	\midrule
72	\multicolumn{4}{l}{\textit{Instance-level signals (consensus-proximity selection)}} \\
73	SJ           & $0.646 \pm 0.002$ & .68 & 0.386 \\
74	FK           & $0.646 \pm 0.001$ & .79 & --- \\
75	EM           & $0.637 \pm 0.001$ & .45 & 0.372 \\
76	VC           & $0.623 \pm 0.004$ & .26 & 0.359 \\
77	\midrule
78	Single$^\ddagger$ & $0.645 \pm 0.001$ & --- & \textbf{0.404} \\
79	Random           & $0.610 \pm 0.003$ & --- & 0.354 \\
80	\bottomrule
81	\end{tabular}
82	\end{table}
83	
84	Despite strong quality estimation, confidence signals yield limited selection gains (Table~\ref{tab:selection}, Figure~\ref{fig:selection_gap}).
85	Instance-level signals (SJ, FK, EM, VC) assign identical scores to all candidates per input and cannot rank outputs by construction; the key question is whether LP---the only per-sample signal---can exploit the oracle headroom.
86	
87	\paragraph{No significant improvement over single-sample.}
88	On SciERC NER (2-seed sign tests, $n{=}551$), the oracle (0.778) reveals 13.3~pp of headroom above single-sample (0.645), yet LP achieves only 0.647 ($\Delta{=}{+}0.2$~pp, $p{=}0.29$); no signal consistently improves selection ($p{>}0.05$; TOST equivalence holds under all external anchors for LLaMA-CoNLL but varies by configuration, Appendix~\ref{app:tost}).
89	On $^\dagger$RE, the best signal (LP, 0.395) falls below single-sample (0.404), with 18.1~pp unrealized.
90	The pattern holds across CoNLL and WNUT-17 (Table~\ref{tab:cross_selection}).
91	Instance-level signals predict \textit{which inputs} the model handles reliably, not \textit{which output} is best; closing this gap likely requires trained verifiers \cite{cobbe2021verifiers}.\footnote{For negative results (all $p{>}0.05$), uncorrected tests suffice; the sole positive finding (non-tied LP subset, $+2.9$~pp, $p{=}0.004$; \S\ref{sec:discussion}) survives Bonferroni correction over 5 comparisons.}
92	
93	%% ============================================================
94	\subsection{Robustness}
95	\label{sec:robustness_main}
96	
97	Consistency signals are robust across $T{\in}\{0.7, 1.0\}$ with sublinear $N$-scaling gains (Table~\ref{tab:robustness}); LP shows the largest temperature sensitivity ($\Delta\rho{=}{+}0.044$).
98	NER calibration is reasonable (ECE 0.069--0.096); $^\dagger$RE miscalibration (ECE${\leq}$0.339) caps $\rho$ at ${\approx}0.28$ for $N{=}16$ (Appendix~\ref{app:calibration}).

102	\small
103	\caption{Scale ablation: Qwen3-8B vs.\ 4B quality estimation ($\rho$; $N{=}8$, $T{=}1.0$, seed${=}42$). 8B values identical to Table~\ref{tab:quality_estimation}; 4B uses matched evaluation protocol. $^\dagger$Preliminary.}
104	\label{tab:scale_ablation}
105	\begin{tabular}{@{}ll cc r@{}}
106	\toprule
107	& & \textbf{8B} & \textbf{4B} & $\Delta$ \\
108	\midrule
109	CoNLL NER & SJ & .436 & .422 & $-$.014 \\
110	          & FK & .400 & .418 & $+$.018 \\
111	SciERC NER & SJ & .360 & .422 & $+$.062 \\
112	           & FK & .267 & .326 & $+$.059 \\
113	SciERC RE$^\dagger$ & SJ & .250 & .267 & $+$.017 \\
114	           & FK & .275 & .359 & $+$.084 \\
115	\bottomrule
116	\end{tabular}

118	
119	\paragraph{Scale robustness.}
120	Repeating with Qwen3-4B (Table~\ref{tab:scale_ablation}), quality estimation is comparable or improved (mean $|\Delta\rho|{=}0.042$), yet selection remains below single-sample on SciERC ($\Delta$ up to $-3.4$~pp) despite 13.0~pp of oracle headroom, and indistinguishable on CoNLL (${<}0.3$~pp, 1.7~pp headroom). Within the 3B--8B range tested across two model families, task difficulty is a stronger predictor of the gap than model scale.

# Provenance Audit Report (D105)

**Date**: 2026-05-16  
**Auditor**: Worker (automated)  
**Scope**: 3 reported numerical discrepancies between paper and registry

---

## Summary

| ID | Claim | Current Paper Value | Registry Truth | Status |
|----|-------|-------------------|----------------|--------|
| c032 | LP cond RE ρ = 0.002 | **0.011** | 0.0112 | CORRECT (already fixed or misreported) |
| c023 | Q1-Q4 SJ ρ = 0.110→0.473 | **0.110→0.473** | 0.447→0.540 | **DISCREPANCY CONFIRMED** |
| c021 | WNUT SJ ρ = 0.062 | **0.089** | 0.089 | CORRECT (fixed in docs/ version) |

---

## Detailed Findings

### c032: LP Conditional RE ρ (72x差异)

**Reported**: Paper writes 0.002, registry truth is 0.0112  
**Actual finding**: Paper currently writes **0.011**, NOT 0.002

- `docs/paper/sections/experiments.tex:50` — "LP $^\dagger$RE collapses to $\rho{=}0.011$"
- `docs/paper/sections/appendix.tex:137` — figure caption: "LP RE collapses to near-zero ($\rho{=}0.011$)"

**Registry verification** (`exp_012_rerun_1024/report.json`):
```
re_logprob_baseline.conditional.rho = 0.01119 (n=238)
```

**Verdict**: Paper's 0.011 is a correct 3-decimal rounding of 0.01119. No error.

**Wrong-source confirmation**: exp_015 (max_tokens=512) gives cond rho=0.1457 (n=296) — different filtering threshold produces inflated n and different rho, but this value is NOT in the paper.

**Note on "0.002"**: This value was NOT found anywhere in the paper (current or old versions) as LP cond RE ρ. The task description may contain a misattribution. The only 0.002 values in experiments.tex are confidence intervals (±0.002) and unrelated deltas.

---

### c023: Q1-Q4 Stratification SJ ρ — CONFIRMED DISCREPANCY

**Location**: `docs/paper/sections/appendix.tex:150`

**Paper text**:
```latex
For RE, SJ $\rho$ increases monotonically with sentence length 
(Q1: 0.110 $\to$ Q4: 0.473; Fisher $z$-test $p{=}0.004$)
```

**Registry truth** (`exp009_stratification_results.json`, scierc_re, by_sent_len):
```
Q1 (lowest): n=143, sj_rho=0.4472
Q2:          n=151, sj_rho=0.3191
Q3:          n=119, sj_rho=0.4975
Q4 (highest):n=138, sj_rho=0.5401
```

**Discrepancy analysis**:
- Paper Q1=0.110 vs truth Q1=0.447 (4x difference)
- Paper Q4=0.473 vs truth Q4=0.540 (14% off)
- Paper claims "monotonically increasing" — truth is NON-monotonic (Q2 dips to 0.319)
- Paper's Fisher z-test p=0.004 may be valid for the wrong values, not the truth

**Possible confusion sources**:
1. **exp_009_v2** (re_seed42, tertile bins): T1=-0.046, T2=0.138, T3=0.267 — T2≈0.138 is close to 0.110 but not exact
2. **by_greedy_f1 dimension** (RE): values are -0.043, -0.003, 0.006, 0.210 — no match
3. **Different pipeline version**: The values 0.110 and 0.473 may originate from an intermediate analysis with different bin boundaries or conditional filtering not present in the final data

**Root cause hypothesis**: Values likely came from a preliminary analysis run (possibly with quartile boundaries computed on a subset, or from a different stratification variable) and were never reconciled with the final exp009 data.

**Correct text should read**: "For RE, SJ ρ ranges from 0.319 (Q2) to 0.540 (Q4) across sentence-length quartiles (Q1: 0.447); the pattern is non-monotonic."

---

### c021: WNUT SJ ρ

**Reported**: Paper writes 0.062, registry truth is 0.089  
**Actual finding**: Paper **already fixed** to 0.089 in current compilation version.

**Current paper** (`docs/paper/sections/appendix.tex:222`, Table tab:wnut):
```latex
SJ      & .089 & .020 & .517 & .288 & ${<}$1e-7 \\
```

**Registry verification** (`exp003_wnut17_eval/report.json`):
```
correlation_softjaccard_vs_f1_full.rho = 0.08883 (n=689)
correlation_softjaccard_vs_f1_conditional.rho = 0.2884 (n=334)
```

**Old version** (`artifacts/_project/paper/experiments.tex:181`):
```latex
SJ achieves $\rho{=}0.062$ ($p{=}0.106$, not statistically significant)
```

**Verdict**: Already corrected. The old 0.062 (artifacts/ version) was likely from an earlier pilot run (exp003_wnut17_pilot?) or from full-set n=1287 without gold-empty filtering.

---

## TACRED Process Check

```
ps aux | grep tacred → No matches
```

No TACRED-related processes running on autodl-5090. The `exp_tacred_re_benchmark` in registry has status=PREPARING, conclusion=killed.

---

## Action Items

| Priority | Item | Action Required |
|----------|------|----------------|
| HIGH | c023 (appendix.tex:150) | Fix Q1-Q4 values to match registry truth. Remove "monotonically increasing" claim. Consider whether to report quartiles (non-monotonic) or focus on Q1 vs Q4 comparison only. |
| NONE | c032 | No action needed — paper is correct (0.011 ≈ 0.0112). |
| NONE | c021 | No action needed — already fixed in docs/ compilation version. |
| LOW | Constraint C001 reminder | Confirm artifacts/_project/paper/ files are NOT used in compilation. They contain stale values (0.062 for WNUT). |

---

## Data Provenance Chain

```
exp_012_rerun_1024 (max_tokens=1024, n_cond=238) → LP RE cond ρ=0.0112 → paper: 0.011 ✓
exp009_stratification_results.json (by_sent_len, scierc_re) → Q1=0.447, Q4=0.540 → paper: 0.110, 0.473 ✗
exp003_wnut17_eval (n=689, gold-filtered) → SJ ρ=0.089 → paper: 0.089 ✓
```
